diagrams.title: Supported actions: authorize before simulator execution
steps: Propose a registered tool action, request data is untrusted
Verify identity and required origin evidence, validate and normalize
Evaluate current tool, arguments, target and available sequence context
BLOCK: no permit or dispatch. SANITIZE: derive a new action and evaluate again.
APPROVAL: persist pending, require distinct review, then explicit owner resume. ALLOW: continue.
Verify the exact permit and claim single use before any target effect
Invoke only the fixed simulator after authorization and claim
Record outcome separately, the read-only console queries bounded projections
Configured-path control only. No real target credentials, universal agent interception or host-wide anti-bypass.

diagrams.title: Flow 1: bounded read allowed by policy
steps: Propose aws.logs.filter_log_events with a bounded limit
Authenticate and verify the source proof when the CLI profile requires it
Construct the canonical action and evaluate the active policy
ALLOW: issue and verify an exact short-lived permit, claim single use
Invoke the simulator with the verified action, not a credential-bearing cloud API
Return up to the requested number of matching simulated log events
Persist bounded decision and outcome evidence in the selected profile
Return the MCP result, the console is outside the execution path

diagrams.title: Flow 2: authenticated destructive proposal blocked
steps: Propose aws.ec2.terminate_instances on a simulated instance
Authenticate, validate and evaluate the canonical action
Record the policy denial without an execution permit or target attempt
The simulator is not invoked. Valid identity does not authorize every action.

diagrams.title: Flow 3: Codex request, human review, explicit resume
steps: After token, enrollment, scope and policy checks, store pending plus exact snapshot
Return approvalRequestId, requestHash, pending and not_executed
Sign in separately, review exact arguments and submit hash-bound decision with CSRF
Verify distinct current human reviewer and atomically record approve or deny
Approved is still not_executed, there is no automatic dispatch
tracepermit_resume_approval: original ID plus requestHash, no replacement arguments
Recheck owner, client, origin, reviewer, policy, expiry and immutable action
Verify permit, atomically consume approval and claim execution
Invoke the approved simulator action only after the claim commits
Return consumed / succeeded, replay cannot dispatch again
Self-review, wrong hash/owner/client, revoked reviewer, expiry or stale policy: reject before dispatch.

diagrams.title: Flow 4: derive, re-evaluate, then authorize
steps: Propose a simulated log read with limit 500 (valid schema, oversized window)
Run only bounded-log-read/v1, clamp limit to 100
Return new event identity and original/effective hash linkage
Re-evaluate the effective action, sanitization is not permission
ALLOW the bounded derived request under current policy
Issue and verify effective-action permit, claim once, then read
Return up to 100 matching simulated events plus sanitization summary
Unknown transformer, invalid output or failed re-evaluation: no dispatch. Limit 50000 fails schema validation.

diagrams.title: Flow 5: synthetic read followed by external-send denial
steps: After allow, record authorized read proposal for tenant plus verified subject
Execute permit-bound fixed read, receive 20 invented records
Independently signed demo.egress.send_external after the read
Neither send reaches the outbox. Sequence history adds a specific reason, not permission to send without history.

diagrams.title: Flow 6: endpoint evidence bound to request and credential
steps: Send strict MCP JSON-RPC over stdio, no trusted identity fields in arguments
Observe immediate parent, executable hash/start time, device and terminal facts
Sign short-lived Ed25519 proof bound to canonical MCP request and bearer fingerprint
Check observed process stability immediately before forwarding
POST exact loopback /mcp with bearer and separate source-attestation header
Authenticate, verify enrolled key, audience, time, request/credential bindings and single use
Build canonical action with bounded verified source facts, then evaluate policy
Invalid or replayed proof stops before protected tool dispatch. A valid proof still does not authorize an action.
Development origin evidence only. This is not the separate bearer-only Codex approval profile or managed-device assurance.

diagrams.title: Flow 7: hosted model proposes, OAuth attributes, tunnel carries
steps: Send prompt to provider backend, the hosted model proposes a configured MCP tool
During app connection, obtain a TracePermit resource access token through OAuth
Return issuer-signed access token, TracePermit does not receive the IdP password
Send MCP proposal and bearer through the configured private tunnel
Verify issuer, signature, audience, time, client, tenant mapping and scopes before dispatch
Normalize authenticated subject and asserted provider actor, evaluate the tool action
Return allowed simulated read or blocked/not_executed destruction
Display the tool result in the unmodified hosted client
One Auth0 + ChatGPT + tunnel profile qualified. Reachability is not identity, endpoint proof or provider-plan attribution.

diagrams.title: Flow 8: signed child authority must narrow its parent
steps: Supply action-bound workload credential and signed parent grant
Supply child grant linked to the exact signed parent hash
Verify trusted issuers/keys, signatures, action context, audience, expiry and chain links
Require child scopes/resources to be subsets and lifetime not to exceed parent
Valid narrowed chain: construct canonical action, then evaluate organizational policy
Only a separate allow plus verified permit enables one simulated read
Separate negative cases: widen scope, resource, audience or lifetime. Reject before canonical policy evaluation.
These are identity-boundary failures, not policy-block results. Causal lineage alone grants no authority.

diagrams.title: Flow 9: lost completion is not permission to repeat
steps: Commit approval consumption and executing claim before dispatch
Attempt separate completion write after simulator dispatch
On completion failure, make one bounded UNKNOWN recording attempt without retrying the effect
Keep committed terminal outcomes. Persistent database failure can still leave the attempt executing.
Return safe error, not invented failure or success, inspect durable status
After restart, attempt resume of the same approval
Reject redispatch because the authority is already consumed
Separate tested recovery foundation: only persisted UNKNOWN attempts enter the leased lookup worker.
Lease unknown candidates bound to tenant, adapter and idempotency identity
Perform reviewed read-only outcome lookup, never invoke the original effect
Append terminal outcome only when confirmed, otherwise defer and remain unknown
No automatic executing-to-unknown sweep or worker is wired into the browser approval launcher, real-target lookup remains future work.

diagrams.title: Flow 10: sign in, then inspect role-scoped approval history
steps: Start sign-in on the numeric-loopback approval origin
Redirect with browser-bound state, nonce and S256 PKCE
Complete sign-in with the configured identity provider
Browser returns the authorization code and issuer
After checking state, exchange code and verify signed access and ID tokens
Set an opaque session cookie, reusable provider tokens stay server-side
Request exact metadata filters and a bounded page using the current session
Recheck token, membership, role, scopes and tenant/owner before querying
Return safe-rendered history and cursor, reading grants no execution authority
Synthetic browser profile is qualified. This is not a new live external-IdP or public browser qualification.

diagrams.title: Flow 11: offline check, explicit initialization, strict startup
steps: Run --check with private configuration, key files and bundled assets
Report offline validity only, no database, IdP traffic or listener
For first installation only, explicitly run --init-db
Hold the initialization lock and install only into a fresh empty dedicated schema
Run --run using the same operator-owned configuration
Validate existing schema and recovery state, never implicitly migrate or repair
Bind 127.0.0.1 and compose authenticated API, optional inbox and approval MCP
Normal runtime needs operator OIDC and PostgreSQL. The synthetic source demo is a different test composition.
An archive manifest identifies a clean source build, not signed provenance or production readiness.

diagrams.title: Flow 12: inspect stored state and explicitly quarantine new authority
steps: First stop agents and effectful services independently. Quarantine cannot cancel already committed claims.
Read aggregate stored-state counts in one read-only snapshot
Return bounded counts, not target outcome proof or permission to resume
Explicitly run --quarantine-db against the intended simulator database
Serialize and commit the one-way recovery guard transition
Attempt a new authority claim or approval review after quarantine
Refuse new authority writes, previous claim completion remains possible
Attempt --run against an already quarantined database
Refuse startup, no resume or quarantine-clear command is provided
An older restored ready row is not detected automatically. This is declared containment, not a restore fence.
